question: Should `tool-progress` become a durable generic public Plugin SDK reply-payload contract shared by producer and channel plugins?
rationale: The bug fix crosses the Codex and Slack plugin boundary, so a public SDK seam is architecturally plausible, but adding permanent third-party API surface requires explicit maintainer ownership and cannot be inferred from tests or contributor proof alone.

options.title: Approve the generic SDK contract
options.body: Keep the new public constant and predicate, require Slack native-block enforcement and compatibility coverage, and document the contract as channel-agnostic transient progress.

options.title: Keep the signal internal
options.body: Replace the public exports with an approved private runtime seam, accepting that bundled producer-to-channel coordination will need a different owner boundary.

options.title: Extend existing progress metadata
options.body: Generalize the already-shipped fast-mode progress contract instead of adding a parallel tool-progress API.

recommendation.title: Approve the generic SDK contract
recommendation.body: Keep the new public constant and predicate, require Slack native-block enforcement and compatibility coverage, and document the contract as channel-agnostic transient progress.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored and merged the current delivery and reply-payload architecture that determines both the Slack behavior and appropriate SDK owner boundary.
